title: Poland asks NATO for F-35s and AWACS after Russian missiles land on its soil
dek: Warsaw calls the Kh-101 missiles and drone that fell during a huge attack on Ukraine a deliberate provocation, but has not invoked Article 4. Moscow has not commented.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone came down inside Poland early on Friday during one of the largest Russian air attacks on Ukraine since the full-scale invasion began in 2022, Poland's defence minister said. Nobody was hurt and no infrastructure was destroyed, but Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incursion "does not look like an accident" and called it an "intentional provocation" by Russia.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned what he called "grave violations" of Polish airspace and said allied jets had been scrambled. Poland has formally asked NATO for more fighter jets and surveillance aircraft under the alliance's eastern air-defence mission, but has stopped short of invoking Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty. Russia had not commented on the incident by Saturday afternoon IST, according to reports.

## What happened

Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz told a press conference in Warsaw that a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile had landed in a field near the village of Nowy Lipowiec, in Biłgoraj county of the Lublin region, about 60 km from the Ukrainian border. The object fell several hundred metres from buildings, near a forest, and caught fire, leaving a crater, according to reports. Police said there was no threat to nearby residents.

A second object, which the minister said was probably also a missile, fell near Rudnik nad Sanem, about 50 km to the west. Infrastructure Minister Dariusz Klimczak said a loud bang had been heard near railway premises there; no visible damage to the tracks was found, but an inspection vehicle was sent. The third object, which came down at Mołodycz, was most likely a jet-powered drone, Mr Kosiniak-Kamysz said. "Nobody was hurt, we did not note any infrastructure destruction," he said.

Poland's Operational Command said it had activated fighter aircraft and ground-based air defences from about 3.30 am local time (8 am IST) as a "preventive" measure because of Russian strikes on western Ukraine, and air-raid alerts were issued in the Lublin and Subcarpathian regions. Mr Tusk said he had been told of an airspace violation just before 8 am local time (12.30 pm IST). Air traffic controllers at Rzeszów airport, the main hub for Western aid to Ukraine, were evacuated and flights were suspended for a time, according to reports.

Mr Tusk later met ministers, military commanders and the heads of the intelligence services. President Karol Nawrocki was briefed.

## Poland's request to NATO

Later on Friday Mr Kosiniak-Kamysz said Poland had formally asked Mr Rutte to allocate additional forces under Operation Eastern Sentry, the air-defence mission NATO set up on its eastern flank after the drone incursion of September 2025, according to reports. The request named F-35 fighter jets and AWACS-type airborne early-warning aircraft to extend radar coverage over eastern Poland. Warsaw also held urgent consultations with allies.

Poland did not invoke Article 4, which lets any member call formal consultations of all allies when it feels its territory or security is threatened, as it did in September 2025. Some early reports said it had; at least one outlet later corrected its headline. Article 5, the alliance's mutual-defence clause, is not triggered automatically by such incidents.

Hours before the objects fell, US President Donald Trump said in an interview that Mr Putin had sent drones and "a couple of little missiles" into Poland "by mistake", according to reports, a view at odds with Warsaw's assessment that the latest incursion was deliberate.

## Why Poland calls it deliberate

Both Mr Tusk and Mr Kosiniak-Kamysz linked the incursion to military exercises by the European-led Coalition of the Willing, the group of countries preparing to support Ukraine after any ceasefire, which are being held in Poland near the impact sites with British and French troops taking part. The timing was "no coincidence", the defence minister said. "We are dealing with yet another provocation by Russia," he said.

> "This incident is clearly dangerous – a consequence of Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine." – NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte

Mr Rutte is expected in Warsaw on Saturday. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha also condemned the violation of Polish airspace.

## The attack on Ukraine

The incursion came during a night-long Russian bombardment that followed President Vladimir Putin's promise of a "far more painful" response to Ukraine's repeated strikes on the Crimean bridge. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had fired more than 400 attack drones and over 110 missiles, "one of the largest attacks" of the war. Ukraine's air force said the barrage included 84 cruise missiles and 404 drones as well as ballistic and Zircon hypersonic missiles, according to reports; it did not give the number of Zircons. Russia said it had used "high-precision" land, sea and air-launched weapons and drones against military-industrial sites and transport infrastructure, including bridges in Kyiv. Neither side's figures can be independently verified.

In Kyiv, missiles damaged three bridges over the Dnipro and cut power, heat and water in parts of the city. Ukraine's emergency service later put the death toll in the capital at six, with about 15 injured, according to reports; earlier official figures said three. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the strikes had damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv, and France has asked for a meeting of the UN Security Council, according to reports. Strikes were also reported in Lviv, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk region and Zaporizhzhia.

## Background

Russian drones and missiles have strayed into the airspace of NATO's eastern members many times since 2022. In November 2022 a missile that killed two people in the Polish village of Przewodów turned out to be a Ukrainian air-defence missile. In September 2025 about 20 Russian drones crossed into Poland, and Warsaw invoked Article 4. This year a Kh-101 exploded in eastern Poland in July, a jet-powered drone hit a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train in September, and a Russian military helicopter briefly crossed from Kaliningrad the same month, according to reports.

The Kh-101 is a long-range, air-launched cruise missile that entered Russian service in 2012 and is designed to fly low to avoid radar.

## Why it matters for India

Any direct clash between Russia and NATO would sharpen the choices facing India, which buys large volumes of Russian crude oil and defence equipment while deepening ties with the US and Europe. India has repeatedly called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war. The incident also comes a day after Mr Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping issued a joint "Declaration towards Peace" in Shenzhen. The Ministry of External Affairs had not commented on the strikes or the incursion by Friday evening.

## What happens next

Polish investigators are examining the three sites and will try to recover debris that can confirm the type and origin of each object. NATO has not yet said whether it will send the extra aircraft Poland has asked for. Mr Rutte is expected in Poland this weekend, and France has asked for a meeting of the UN Security Council over the strikes on Kyiv; no date had been announced by Saturday afternoon. The European Union said it would summon Russia's ambassador over the strikes, according to reports. Moscow has not said whether it accepts responsibility for the objects that fell in Poland.

## Key numbers

- 2 Russian missiles and 1 drone fell in Poland, according to Poland's defence minister
- 60 km: distance of the Nowy Lipowiec impact site from the Ukrainian border
- 110+ missiles and 400+ drones fired at Ukraine overnight, according to President Zelensky
- 6 killed in Kyiv, according to Ukraine's emergency service, as cited in reports (preliminary)
- 0 injuries in Poland
